/v/socialskills is fundamentally an experiment. On Reddit, /r/socialskills is a pretty good site for beginners, but it isn't very good for getting past that. This subverse is tightly moderated to try to improve the content quality. Not everyone will like this, so I've also created /v/socialskillsopen.

This is an innovative system that limits mod power. Every month (every week once more content is posted), there will be a mod post linking to the top voted articles in /v/socialskillsopen. This means that if the community disagrees with a moderation decision, that that content will likely be posted by somone to /v/socialskillsopen and heavily upvoted, leading to subscribers in the main sub to be able to see it in the next summary post.

I have two months worth of content ready to go to seed this sub. I'll be making at least one post every day.

I think that is it very important to define the type of content that we want to try to encourage in this sub. I want this sub to be useful, not just to beginners, but to people who have been working on this for a long time. This is the kind of content that I am going to work hard to produce and try to support:

  • Any content containing original ideas or techniques
  • Psychological research related to social skills
  • Videos showing examples of good conversational technique
  • Lessons learned after undertaking a particular activity to try to improve you socially
  • Summaries of the different kinds of advice given for a particular problem
  • Specific questions that have not been asked before directly or not satisfactorily answered by a more general question
  • Reviews of a book/resource or detailed summaries of the main points
  • Links to high quality resources (generally with an explanation of what the resource offers)
